Details.Name: Compromise of Battery Pack Parameters
Details.Description: An attacker modifies critical parameters of the BatteryPack, such as charge/discharge limits or temperature thresholds, leading to unsafe operation, potential battery damage, or reduced lifespan. This can be achieved by exploiting vulnerabilities in the communication protocols or by unauthorized access to the BMS firmware.

Details.Name: Tampering with Cell Monitoring Data
Details.Description: An attacker injects false data into the CellMonitoring system, reporting incorrect cell voltages or temperatures. This can lead the BMS to make incorrect decisions regarding cell balancing, charging, or thermal management, potentially causing battery imbalance, overheating, or reduced performance.

Details.Name: Firmware Modification
Details.Description: An attacker gains unauthorized access to the Code Flash and modifies the BMS firmware. This could disable safety features, introduce malicious code for lateral movement, or cause complete system failure. This is often achieved by exploiting vulnerabilities in update mechanisms or by compromising debug interfaces.

Details.Name: Manipulation of Calibration Data
Details.Description: An attacker alters calibration data stored in Data Flash. This could include modifying parameters related to battery health assessment, charging profiles, or thermal management, leading to incorrect operation, reduced battery lifespan, or safety hazards.

Details.Name: Key Exposure
Details.Description: Cryptographic keys stored in the Keys component are exfiltrated. This compromises the security of the entire system, allowing attackers to impersonate the BMS, decrypt sensitive communications, or bypass authentication mechanisms.

Details.Name: Debug Port Exploitation
Details.Description: An attacker gains unauthorized access to the Debug Port to manipulate firmware, extract sensitive data, or gain control of the BMS. This can lead to a complete compromise of the system and potentially influence vehicle behavior.

Details.Name: CAN Bus Spoofing (ICD Shunt CAN)
Details.Description: An attacker injects false current shunt data onto the ICD Shunt CAN bus. This misleads the BMS about the actual current flowing, potentially causing inaccurate State of Charge (SoC) and State of Health (SoH) calculations, and leading to inefficient or unsafe battery operation.

Details.Name: False SoC/SoH Reporting
Details.Description: An attacker manipulates the State of Charge (SoC) and State of Health (SoH) data. This can lead to misleading information for the user, potentially causing range anxiety or overestimation of battery life, and can impact warranty claims or resale value.

Details.Name: Vehicle CAN Bus Attack
Details.Description: An attacker compromises the Vehicle CAN bus connection to the BMS. This could involve injecting false commands, flooding the bus with messages, or modifying critical data, leading to erratic vehicle behavior, loss of control, or system failures.

Details.Name: Cloud Data Exfiltration
Details.Description: Sensitive battery operational data or user-related information stored in the cloud is accessed and exfiltrated by an attacker. This could include detailed battery performance logs, charging patterns, or potentially linked user data.

requirements.name: Secure Debug Port Access
requirements.description: Implement robust authentication and authorization mechanisms for the debug port. Disable it completely in production unless absolutely necessary and protected by strong security measures.

requirements.name: Secure Firmware Update Verification
requirements.description: Implement secure boot and firmware signing with strong cryptographic algorithms to prevent the execution of unauthorized or tampered firmware.

requirements.name: CAN Bus Message Authentication
requirements.description: Utilize message authentication codes (MACs) and sequence counters (e.g., SecOC) for critical CAN messages to prevent spoofing and ensure data integrity.

requirements.name: Physical Security Measures
requirements.description: Ensure physical enclosures of the BMS prevent unauthorized access to internal components like the debug port. Tamper-evident seals can also be employed.

requirements.name: Secure Cloud Communication
requirements.description: Encrypt all data transmitted to and from the cloud using industry-standard protocols (e.g., TLS/SSL) and implement access controls on cloud-based data storage.

requirements.name: Diagnostic Service Authentication
requirements.attack_scene: Abuse Standard Diagnostic Protocol for Data Collection (SoC/SoH)
requirements.description: Implement strong authentication (e.g., Seed/Key mechanism) for accessing sensitive diagnostic services that could reveal or manipulate SoC/SoH data.

requirements.name: Integrity Protection for Battery Parameters
requirements.description: Employ checksums, CRCs, or authenticated encryption for critical battery parameters stored or transmitted to detect and prevent unauthorized modifications.

requirements.name: Input Validation for Cell Monitoring Data
requirements.description: Implement sanity checks and range validation for all incoming cell monitoring data to detect anomalies or malicious injections.

requirements.name: Secure Storage of Calibration Data
requirements.description: Use write protection mechanisms and integrity checks (e.g., CRC) for critical calibration data stored in non-volatile memory.

requirements.name: Hardware-Based Key Protection
requirements.description: Store cryptographic keys in a Hardware Security Module (HSM) or a secure element that prevents their extraction or direct access by software.

requirements.name: CAN Bus Integrity for Vehicle Communication
requirements.description: Implement end-to-end protection or MACs for critical CAN messages exchanged on the vehicle network to ensure integrity and authenticity.
